text:
incident_bot: :rotating_light: P1 alert — Auth-proxy: sudden inbound surge of invalid token attempts. Source cluster of IPs starting with 34.65.12.*. Rate ~12k req/min, 94% 401s. Detected 2024-05-12T03:12Z by rate-anom rule. Auto-throttle engaged.

incident_bot: sample logs:
```
2024-05-12T03:11:52Z auth-proxy-12 ERROR invalid_token client_id=svc-metrics src=34.65.12.8 ua="curl/7.85"
2024-05-12T03:11:53Z auth-proxy-12 ERROR invalid_token client_id=svc-metrics src=34.65.12.9
... repeated 12000x/min ...
```

ryan_oncall: acked. investigating. I'll look at WAF rules + gateway ACLs. @tahira you oncall for infra?

tahira: oncall. I'll start with a quick block at edge and check whether these IPs resolve to a cloud provider or legit customer.

ryan_oncall: good plan. can we add a temporary denylist for 34.65.12.0/24 at the LB? Doing it now.

devops_bot: applied ACL rule: `deny 34.65.12.0/24` to prod-edge-lb-1 (rule id acl-20240512-17). propagation ~30s.

maria_g: any customer-facing errors? I'm seeing increased 401s in the last 5m for token-introspect endpoint. No 500s. Customers A and C show spike in failed auths, likely retries.

ryan_oncall: confirmed. 401s up +22% for token-introspect; latency steady. looks like replay/fuzzing rather than service-side crash.

paul_prodsec: quick check: do we think tokens were leaked or is this just credential stuffing from external list? Any logs showing valid JWTs rejected vs malformed?

ryan_oncall: majority are malformed/expired. a small fraction (~0.6%) are syntactically valid but fail signature. My read: credential stuffing using guessed tokens and replay of expired ones. No sign of successful auth.

paul_prodsec: ok. low likelihood of successful exfil but still treat as suspicious. Recommend: 1) blacklist source netblocks for now, 2) rotate service principal keys used by public SDKs (svc-public-*), 3) force short session revocation for affected client IDs, 4) open a tracking incident ticket with cust-impact notes.

tahira: starting rotation plan for svc-public-1 keys. We'll do canary rotation for 5% of tokens first, watch error rate. Steps in runbook:
```
- create new key pair in KMS for svc-public-1
- stage new key in auth-signing service (canary namespace)
- update internal routing for key id -> canary
- wait 2m, monitor token-verify error rate
- roll forward or rollback
```

ryan_oncall: I'll follow the runbook and coordinate maintenance window with SRE. Starting now — creating key.

devops_bot: ticket created: INC-20240512-4315 "Auth inbound rate anomaly — mitigate & rotate keys". Pagerduty incident linked.

maria_g: heads-up to support: tickets may come in from customers seeing 401s. Message template: short note, we're aware and mitigating, recommend retry/backoff, no confirmed data loss.

paul_prodsec: also advise product teams to watch third-party integrations; some token refresh loops could be amplifying load. Suggest temporarily increasing client-side backoff in docs and SDKs.

ryan_oncall: can confirm we saw a few SDKs doing tight refresh loops after 401s. Pushing a quick advisory to SDK teams now.

tahira: can we revoke refresh tokens for compromised client IDs? We should only do targeted revokes. Which client IDs are noisy?

ryan_oncall: top noisy client_ids: svc-metrics, sdk-demo-1, mobile-internal-test. I'll mark svc-metrics for targeted refresh-token revoke after canary key is validated (to avoid breaking legitimate flows).

paul_prodsec: agreed. targeted revocation + key rotation is good balance. Also run a quick search for suspicious log export operations — ensure there wasn't an accidental log push that could have leaked tokens.

ryan_oncall: checked logs S3 PUTs in last 24h: no anomalous cross-account copies. No internal pipeline jobs matching that IP range.

maria_g: support notified and draft prepared. Customer-facing line: "We're investigating increased failed auth attempts that may lead to transient 401s. We're actively mitigating and will provide updates shortly. No evidence of successful access."

devops_bot: canary key deployed to auth-signing-canary (svc-public-1) — health checks green. Monitoring 2m.

ryan_oncall: canary looks stable. token-verify errors unchanged for unaffected clients, noisy ones down ~60% after ACL. I'll proceed with staged rotation across 3% -> 20% -> 100% over next 30m windows unless we see regressions.

tahira: I'll prep next-oncall handoff notes. If we need full key rotation runbook, grab DOCS/RUNBOOKS#auth-rotate.

paul_prodsec: assign action items:
- ryan_oncall: complete staged rotation, targeted revokes for noisy client_ids, update incident ticket with timeline
- tahira: monitor edge ACL and LB health, escalate to network team if propagation issues
- maria_g: update support and engineering comms, prepare postmortem stub
- paul_prodsec: coordinate with compliance if any customer requests come in

ryan_oncall: handing off monitoring to @tahira in 30m window. I'll stay available for questions but moving to follow-up tasks. Summary for next oncall: edge ACL applied, canary key healthy, staged rotation in progress, no confirmed data exfil, targeted revokes pending.

tahira: ack. I'll take it from here, will ping if traffic resurges or we see any sign of successful auth.

incident_bot: incident status updated to "mitigating". Next update in 15m or on significant event. :lock:

paul_prodsec: please attach list of noisy client_ids and final rotation timeline to INC-20240512-4315 before the handoff completes.

ryan_oncall: will add. closing active paging for now — leaving incident in mitigating state.
